A raw pin into one clk flop, with no synchroniser. There are at least 80 ns to the next edge for an output to resolve before anything reads it, and pll_en is a slow enable (REQ-CTRL-REG). If it did not resolve in time it could mis-set wd_cnt, stretching a recovery to at most about 1024 reference cycles, which then ends on its own. Qualitative: no MTBF.

Not quasi-static: n_sel is a raw pin that REQ-LOOP-RELOCK changes live. A change between the clk_pre edges, or an intermediate code or bounce, can give one extra or missing clk_fb edge per transition without any metastability. Accepted because no div_cnt state stalls (the >= compare wraps from every state, n_m1 <= 4) and exact N returns within N clk_pre periods; the worst effect at the outputs is a lock drop and a relock. Cosim changes n_sel on clk falling edges only and only a few times.

Same pin. n_sel reaches clk_fb only through fb_en, which is clocked on the falling edge of clk_pre. A runt on clk_fb needs metastability that outlasts the clk_pre low phase (at least 10.8 ns at the 5.4 ns vco_div2 period), and it costs one bad edge that the PFD then corrects like any other phase error. Qualitative: no MTBF is computed.

A single-flop sample on purpose: wide_q is the half-period threshold of a lock indicator. It has half a reference period to resolve (40 ns at 12.5 MHz, assuming 50% duty on clk). In lock the pulses sit far from the sample point, so an ambiguous sample means the pulse is about T/2, the threshold itself, and either answer is right. Even unresolved it only masks count+1 in lock_cnt, so the count cannot inflate: the worst effect is a late or dropped lock, not a false one.

waived.msg: u_pfd.pfd_dn (vco_div2) -> u_pfd.pfd_ref_q (clk): async reset, 1 bit path(s)
waived.reason: The PFD's function (REQ-PFD-RESET): both flops high clear each other through two delay cells. Every state is legal and 11 self-clears, so there is no lock-up. A recovery violation or an edge lost to the clear costs one reference cycle of phase error. Formal cuts these flops (spec.yaml async_reset_cuts); the evidence is gate-level cosim, with no metastability model.

waived.msg: reset rst_n releases 22 flop(s) in domain clk (clock nets u_ctrl.clk) with no reset synchroniser in that domain
waived.reason: Accepted with no synchroniser. At the first edge after release the multi-bit registers' D equals their reset value (wide_q = 1 forces lock_cnt's next value to 0, pll_en = 0 clears wd_cnt), so only wide_q, pll_en, cp_trim0/1 and pfd_ref_q can slip, each by one cycle and independently of the others, and each of those is a state that resolves on the next clk edge. rst_n -> clk recovery slack is not established.

waived.msg: reset rst_n releases 8 flop(s) in domain vco_div2 (clock nets u_div.clk_fb, u_div.clk_pre, u_pre.pre_q0, u_pre.vco_div2) with no reset synchroniser in that domain
waived.reason: Accepted with no synchroniser. In the final tile pll_en = 0 holds vco_div2, so release after a long enough reset sees a quiet clock; the window exists on the standalone tile and after a short reset. In it a pre_q0 runt can toggle pre_q1, giving a clk_pre/obs_out pulse of about one vco_div2 period minus settling, under one VCO period if settling exceeds 2.7 ns. It clears inside the first clk_pre period, since toggle flops have no illegal state and fb_en cannot be hit until clk_pre has risen and fallen. REQ-DIV-RESET-CLEAN is narrowed to say so, and no test exercises this window. constraints.sdc does not time rst_n recovery to the VCO clocks.

waived.msg: reset net u_pfd.pfd_clr is driven by combinational logic and resets 1 flop(s) in domain clk: a glitch on it resets them
waived.reason: The PFD's clear, combinational by design (REQ-PFD-RESET). rst_n releases with both Qs at 0, so pfd_rst is low and that release is clean. pfd_both glitches only on a metastable Q or a clear's tail, and a spurious clear means state 00 and one truncated pulse, corrected on the next reference cycle. Whether the delay cells filter such a glitch is not established.
